claim: The retention period of a Kinesis data stream is the time from when a record is added to when it is no longer accessible. Data records are stored in the shards of the stream only temporarily.
question: What is the retention period of a Kinesis data stream?

values.display: from when a record is added to when it is no longer accessible
stored in shards in your stream temporarily

evidence.quote: Data records are therefore stored in shards in your stream temporarily. The time period from when a record is added to when it is no longer accessible is called the *retention period*.

claim: When you decrease the retention period, Kinesis Data Streams almost immediately makes records older than the new retention period inaccessible, so be careful with DecreaseStreamRetentionPeriod.
question: What happens to existing records when you decrease the retention period of a Kinesis data stream?

values.display: almost immediately makes records older than the new retention period inaccessible
take great care when calling

evidence.quote: Kinesis Data Streams almost immediately makes records older than the new retention period inaccessible upon decreasing the retention period. Therefore, take great care when calling the [DecreaseStreamRetentionPeriod](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_DecreaseStreamRetentionPeriod.html) operation.

claim: After you increase the retention period, Kinesis Data Streams stops making records inaccessible at the old retention period within several minutes. Records added just before the old limit stay available after it.
question: What happens to records close to expiry when you increase the retention period?

values.display: stops making records inaccessible at the old retention period within several minutes
still available after 24 hours

qualifiers.condition: example in the page: 24 hours changed to 48 hours

evidence.quote: Kinesis Data Streams stops making records inaccessible at the old retention period within several minutes of increasing the retention period. For example, changing the retention period from 24 hours to 48 hours means that records added to the stream 23 hours 55 minutes prior are still available after 24 hours.

claim: Set the Kinesis data retention period so that consumers can read data before it expires if problems occur. Think of the retention period as a safety net that gives data consumers more time to recover.
question: How should you think about the retention period of a Kinesis data stream?

values.display: safety net to allow more time for your data consumers to recover
consumers are able to read data before it expires

evidence.quote: Set your data retention period to ensure that your consumers are able to read data before it expires, if problems occur. You should carefully consider all possibilities, such as an issue with your record processing logic or a downstream dependency being down for a long period of time. Think of the retention period as a safety net to allow more time for your data consumers to recover.

claim: Support for larger records does not change the per-shard limits of 1 MB/s for writes and 2 MB/s for reads. Kinesis Data Streams is designed for intermittent large records next to baseline traffic of 1 MiB or smaller, not for sustained high-volume large record ingestion.
question: Do larger record sizes raise the per-shard throughput limit of Kinesis Data Streams?

values.display: 1 MB/s for writes, and 2 MB/s for reads remain unchanged
not designed to accommodate sustained high-volume large record ingestion

qualifiers.condition: streams that use the larger maximum record size

evidence.quote: Individual shard throughput limit of 1 MB/s for writes, and 2 MB/s for reads remain unchanged with support for larger record sizes. Kinesis Data Streams is designed to accommodate intermittent large records alongside a baseline traffic of records less than, or equal to 1 MiB. It is not designed to accommodate sustained high-volume large record ingestion.

claim: For continuous streams of large records, store the payloads in Amazon S3 and send only metadata references to the Kinesis data stream.

values.display: Store payloads in Amazon S3
send only metadata references to the stream

evidence.quote: Store payloads in Amazon S3 and send only metadata references to the stream for continuous streams of large records.

claim: You can map a Lambda function to a Kinesis Data Streams shared-throughput consumer (standard iterator), or to a dedicated-throughput consumer with enhanced fan-out.
question: Can a Lambda function read from a Kinesis data stream through an enhanced fan-out consumer?

values.display: shared-throughput consumer (standard iterator)
dedicated-throughput consumer with enhanced fan-out

claim: A Lambda enhanced fan-out stream consumer gets a dedicated connection to each shard that does not affect other applications reading the stream, and Kinesis pushes records to Lambda over HTTP/2.
question: How does an enhanced fan-out consumer deliver Kinesis records to Lambda?

values.display: dedicated connection to each shard that doesn't impact other applications
pushing records to Lambda over a long-lived connection

evidence.quote: Enhanced fan-out consumers get a dedicated connection to each shard that doesn't impact other applications reading from the stream. Stream consumers use HTTP/2 to reduce latency by pushing records to Lambda over a long-lived connection and by compressing request headers.

claim: Lambda reads Kinesis records in batches and invokes your function synchronously. Each batch contains records from a single shard of the data stream.
question: Can one Lambda batch from Kinesis contain records of several shards?

values.display: Each batch contains records from a single shard
invokes your function synchronously

evidence.quote: Lambda reads records from the data stream and invokes your function [synchronously](invocation-sync.md) with an event that contains stream records. Lambda reads records in batches and invokes your function to process records from the batch. Each batch contains records from a single shard/data stream.

claim: To increase the speed at which a Lambda function processes Kinesis records, add shards to the data stream. Lambda processes records in each shard in order and stops processing more records in a shard if the function returns an error.
question: How do you speed up Lambda processing of a Kinesis data stream, and what does a function error do?

values.display: add shards to your data stream
stops processing additional records in a shard if your function returns an error

evidence.quote: To increase the speed at which your function processes records, [add shards to your data stream](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/kinesis-data-streams-open-shards). Lambda processes records in each shard in order. It stops processing additional records in a shard if your function returns an error. With more shards, there are more batches being processed at once, which lowers the impact of errors on concurrency.
